name: Date Range Picker
tagline: Pick a start and end date as one range, on a two-month calendar.

limitations: The calendar opens as a floating layer about 340px tall, and the demo runs in an iframe sized to the control's resting height — so the calendar is clipped by the frame rather than floating above the page as it does on a real form. Nothing is stubbed and every interaction works; what is missing is room to see it. Install the solution, or use npm start in the repository, to see the picker at full size.

presets.name: Default
presets.description: The whole picker: click a start, click an end, and the range is drawn between them across two months. Every date is written as noon rather than midnight, because a value that lands on the day boundary reports the wrong calendar day to half the world.

presets.name: Calendar only
presets.description: The quick-range rail switched off, which is what an empty presets list means. The calendar is unchanged; the popover is simply narrower.

presets.name: Single day
presets.description: Start and end on the same day, which this configuration allows. One day is drawn as one shape rather than as a start and an end fighting over the same corner.

presets.name: End before start
presets.description: The validation state, reached by typing rather than by clicking: picking the earlier day second swaps the pair instead of refusing it. The range is shown but never written back, so the columns cannot come to hold a backwards pair.

presets.name: Within bounds
presets.description: Outer limits set, so every day outside them is disabled in the calendar rather than clicked and then refused. Same-day ranges are blocked here as well.

presets.name: Nothing chosen
presets.description: Both columns empty, so the field shows its placeholder. A half-filled pair is not an error, and no message shows until both dates exist.
